correctness.rationale: All four parameter regimes are exhausted by dimension and k=1 cases. For every k>=2,n>=2k, decomposition X+A+B and quotient-lift constructions give all four proper two-point witnesses, including the t=0 boundary. A projective pencil of q+1 k-spaces has an impossible 3-pattern, proved by linear dependence in H/U and independent vectors in C; an explicit rank-four sentence separates the Rado graph. Finite exhaustive/sampled checker corroborates the nonstandard lemmas and the rank-three EF implication is reconstructed.

Related bipartite walk results also do not imply the 3-pencilled forbidden pattern. Inaccessible/unindexed full theorem risk is retained.

value.rationale: The disjointness q-Kneser family is a standard, naturally motivated finite-geometry graph family. The sharp rank-three Rado coincidence at minimum ambient dimension n=2k, versus a universal rank-four pencil obstruction, produces a complete four-type classification and a concrete logical expressivity boundary for all finite fields and every k>=3. Neither arbitrary parameter selection nor textbook cardinality substitution is the source of the result; the quotient and pencil structures are essential.
